title: Chroma VII kinetic installation Yunchul Kim CERN Science Gateway June 2026 (11) Side view
desc_src: "Chroma VII" is a large-scale kinetic and chromatic installation by South Korean transdisciplinary artist Yunchul Kim, created to blur the line between art, philosophy, and quantum physics. Suspended 1.5 meters above the ground, the artwork represents a headless, tailless 8-looped knot, drawing upon the Ouroboros (symbolizing natural cycles and infinity) and String Theory from physics. The organism-like machine, measuring 2.6m x 1.4m, is composed of 162 rings holding transparent polymer scale-cells filled with a custom liquid solvent. As driven by microcontrollers, the mechanical deformation of these cells changes light refraction, making the structure breathe and radiate with luminescent ice-blue, gold, red, and violet hues. Fascinatingly, this mechanical movement is governed by data corresponding to the real-time flow of cosmic muons.

title: MOMACatalog1972-'Kinetic Circle'
desc_src: The Museum of Modern Art New York, Christmas Catalog 1972, pg. 18. Catalog text reads: “Kinetic Circle by Phyllis Mark. This superbly executed multiple sculpture is signed by the artist and produced in a limited edition of 100. Designed for suspension from a lucite display stand, it is also intended to be worn on the accompanying neckband. Made from highly polished 23K heavy gold plate on aluminum, the multiple measures 3 3/4 inches in diameter. The floating center form is threaded with nylon through the circle to create the hanging loop. The stand measures 5 1/4 inches high and the base 5 3/4 x 2 inches. Comes in deep purple flannel bag and gift box: $95 (members $71.25)”
photographer: Phyllis Mark archives. Uploaded by Ira S. Mark, TTEE, Phyllis Mark Revocable Trust, the trust of the late artist's estate.

"Chroma VII" is a large-scale kinetic and chromatic installation by South Korean transdisciplinary artist Yunchul Kim, created to blur the line between art, philosophy, and quantum physics. Suspended 1.5 meters above the ground, the artwork represents a headless, tailless 8-looped knot, drawing upon the Ouroboros (symbolizing natural cycles and infinity) and String Theory from physics. The organism-like machine, measuring 2.6m x 1.4m, is composed of 162 rings holding transparent polymer scale-cells filled with a custom liquid solvent. Fascinatingly, this mechanical movement is governed by data corresponding to the real-time flow of cosmic muons. In the background behind the installation, the flags of CERN member states and the surrounding landscape are visible through the panoramic windows

desc_src: The stainless steel kinetic sculpture "Wellenbinder﻿" ("Wave Binder"), created by German artist Christiane Möbus in 2000. The artwork, with its long, antenna-like rods and curved elements, evokes themes of energy and waves, reflecting the fusion research conducted at the institute

title: Kineic Art WindKutsche
desc_src: de:WindKutsch en:Wind Chariot The WindKutsche resembles a roman chariot. In the stead of a warrior, a tower with a rotor is standing on the axis. The rotation is transmitted by a chain to the head, where an excenter moves a free hanging stick up and down. With the help of this stick the chariot moves stilting against the wind. When the stick has no contact to the ground it is pushed by the wind a little backwards. Than the stick goes down and lifts the head. Now the hole sculpture is standing on the instable stick and two weels. In this way, the sculpture stumbles against the wind.

title: Gábor Szauder Modulator V3, Városházstrasse 9-11, 2024 Belváros-Lipótváros
desc_src: Light Art Museum Budapest (LAM) Gábor Szauder Modulator V3 (first presented at the 2022 exhibition?) is a device for light painting (kinetic sculpture?), which is a recreation of László Moholy-Nagy's work entitled 'Light prop for electric stage' executed in 1930. It was designed by architect István Sebók in Courtyard I. of the Budapest City Hall . Media artist/painter David Szauder (b. 1976) studied Art History at the Eötvös Loránd University and Intermedia at the Hungarian University of Fine Arts in Budapest, and completed a Masters Fellowship at the School of Arts, Design and Architecture at the Aalto University in Helsinki. - 1-3 (1-5) Bárczy Street =2 Gerlóczy Street=9-11 Városház Street, Inner City neighbourhood, District V of Budapest .

title: Keck Center, U.S. National Academies (facade and kinetic sculpture)
desc_src: Keck Center of The U.S. National Academies 500 Fifth Street NW Exterior Opened in 2002, the Keck Center houses more than 1,000 employees and is a popular site for public meetings. Slow Rondo (Kinetic Sculpture), 2002 Don Merkt Stainless Steel, Aluminum and Painted Steel 20’9’H x 18’9”W x 16’D The concept for this kinetic sculpture was motivated by the concerns and activities of the National Academies -- with an emphasis on research. Symbolically it focuses on the analysis of our multi-textured world by an intelligent and compassionate eye. Three concentric circular planes all move independently while sharing the same vertical axis; movements are initiated by the wind. When the wind allows, the circular planes align and combine to form two mosaic images that dominate the sculpture, one side representing the human eye and the other side the cosmos. Inherent in the design are the macro and the micro interests of the National Academies.
